system:
You are the Network operator and regulator reviewer, standing in for the telecom regulator and mobile operators (cell broadcast delivery). You check that the message can be delivered and read on a handset: required languages present, no language over the 15-page cell broadcast maximum, the encoding, and that the first page carries the hazard and the action.
You see only each language's phone text with its character count, encoding and page count, and the profile's required languages. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

[MHEWS-2026#0482] Leveraging AI to Enhance Multi-Hazard Early Warning Systems (full report) (p.115):
must justify their actions to superiors, political authorities, and affected communities. Traditional forecasting systems often allow experts to identify the source of error, whether it is related to incorrect input data, model assumptions, or anomalous environmental conditions. This traceability supports institutional learning and enables users to develop calibrated expectations about system reliability. When AI systems produce unexpected or inaccurate outputs, however, identifying the source of failure may be far more difficult. Without diagnostic clarity, confidence in system reliability becomes fragile. With AI-based early warning systems, the difficulty of tracing back the error (and therefore improving the model output) can result in repeated false alarms. Research has documented “cry wolf” effects: recurring false alarms lead to warning fatigue, where communities become skeptical and less likely to take protective action (Breznitz, 2013). Each false alarm imposes costs on those who comply (Krishnamurthy R et al., 2020). On the other extreme, a false negative whereby an early warning system fails to predict a crisis would result in mistrust of systems. After multiple false alarms or false negatives, early warning systems lose credibility, and relevant actors may stop responding to warnings (Simmons & Sutter, 2009).

data.summary: Delivery checks pass: English is GSM-7, 516 characters, 6 pages, under the 15-page cell broadcast maximum, and the GENERIC profile requires no languages. The first page fails the readability check. At 93 GSM-7 characters per page, page 1 holds only the preamble about the bulletin and the 10 km area. It does not name the hazard (the Pickering incident) or the action (no protective action needed, no abnormal release). The drafter can fix this by reordering the text.

objections.issue: The first cell broadcast page (93 GSM-7 characters) does not carry the hazard or the action. Page 1 reads roughly 'This is a Province of Ontario emergency bulletin which applies to people within ten (10) kil'. The incident and the key instruction ('DO NOT need to take any protective actions', 'NO abnormal release') do not appear until pages 2-5. A reader who sees only page 1 learns there is an emergency near a nuclear station but not what happened or what to do. That invites alarm and calls.
objections.fix: Put the hazard and action in the first 93 characters. For example: 'Pickering Nuclear Station incident: NO radioactive release. NO action needed by public now.' Then follow with the area (within 10 km) and the media instruction. Keep the total at 15 pages or fewer.
